measurement_method: Read all three components in full; identified the shared move/engine/end loop surface and the per-component divergences. Line counts via wc -l.

duplicated_loop_surface.description: The onMove -> (move + reassign fen + lastMove) -> checkEnd -> engineMove -> (pick + moveUci + reassign fen + lastMove) -> checkEnd loop, plus turnColor(), the ADR-0051 in-check derived + its 4-line comment, illegal-engine-move halt, resign-during-think guard, and the over-state guard.

shared_functions_reimplemented_in_all_th.identical: same skeleton; Play adds playedUci + coached pre-check
same skeleton; Play adds clock budget + book move + style branch + retry; siblings call pickMove(fen,500)
same terminal()->status/result skeleton; Play folds the game (rating/persist), siblings only set result + resultKind
same shape; Play stops clock + finishGame('loss')
same 'engine returned illegal -> status=over' guard, comment cross-refs P1-17

duplicated_loop_surface.estimated_duplicated_logic_lines_per_sib: ~55-70 lines of move/engine/end loop in each of Sparring & Comeback are near-verbatim of each other (the two WEAK copies are ~90% identical to one another); Play is the superset.
duplicated_loop_surface.sparring_vs_comeback_diff: Sparring and Comeback loops differ only in: i18n key prefix (sparring.* vs comeback.*), seed source (Scenario vs ComebackPosition), playerSide source (sideToTrain vs playerColor), and the draw label semantics (drawn/good vs heldDraw/good). The MOVE/ENGINE/END mechanics are otherwise identical.

behaviour_to_preserve_exactly: Play: clock budget (botMovetime), pickHumanMove vs pickMove by opponentStyle, retry on engine error, coached takeback, 960 fenForEngine routing, opening book move, rating fold + persist, FIDE 6.9 flag resolution.
Sparring: untimed, pickMove(fen,500) only (engine style, fixed movetime), NO persistence, resultKind good/bad, draw='drawn'(good).
Comeback: untimed, pickMove(fen,500) only, NO persistence, resultKind good/bad, draw='heldDraw'(good), idx/next-position flow.

tests_present.board_reactivity: src/ui/board-reactivity.test.ts via makeBoardState (ADR-0051 staleness regression) — DOM-free harness pattern

tests_absent_CRITICAL.component_level: NO test mounts or imports Play.svelte / Sparring.svelte / Comeback.svelte. grep for 'Play.svelte|mount(|render(' in *.test.ts = 0 matches.
tests_absent_CRITICAL.implication: There is NO existing behaviour test of the triplicated loop at the component level. The parity gate CANNOT lean on existing component tests. The refactor MUST extract the loop into a DOM-free, unit-testable controller core (mirroring playSession.ts + board-reactivity.svelte.ts) so behaviour parity is PROVABLE. This is the single most important design constraint for this PR.

purity_constraints.impure_dependencies: AdaptiveOpponent.pickHumanMove uses Math.random; clock loop uses performance.now (Play only). The controller core takes these via injection (engine client + a now()/movetime provider) so the core stays testable; the Svelte component supplies the rAF/clock + DOM.
